decision: Round cap (3) reached. Round-3 verdict PENDING-JUDGMENT, evals 12/12 PASS, but 3 new confirmed findings (1 HIGH, 1 MED, 1 LOW carried). Per feature-loop rules: STOP, do NOT auto-fix into round 4, escalate to human with per-round analysis. Contract remains status:implemented; verified NOT set; no signoff.

HIGH confirmed independently by main loop: the round-2 within-place_rank importance comparator in src/lib/geocoding.ts:149 is non-transitive (cmp(A,C)=0, cmp(C,B)=0, cmp(A,B)!=0). Reproduced: same 3 elements in 3 different input orders yield 3 different results[0] (rural street / whole city / correct boulevard). The round-2 fix for the Nguyen Hue bug is itself order-dependent.

Root cause is a test-design gap, not 3 unrelated bugs: every geocoding/region test mocks fetch and returns a fixed array, so ranking order and the region path's real behaviour are asserted nowhere. check-vn-addresses.ts probes resolveLocation only, never resolveBoundary. Each round's local patch to the ranking heuristic spawned the next round's HIGH.

Human (manh) authorised exceeding the 3-round cap with a SCOPED round 4: (1) HIGH — replace the non-transitive comparator with a real total order + permutation test; (2) MED — route region strings through normalize + city-guard + osm_id lookup, add a live resolveBoundary probe; (3) LOW — add Origin/Host validation to the HTTP transport (human chose fix over accept). Explicit goal: close the test-design gap (mocks never assert ordering) that generated the round-2 and round-3 HIGHs.

HIGH R3#1 fixed: replaced the non-transitive comparator in src/lib/geocoding.ts with rankThenImportance() — bucket by place_rank (Map preserves first-seen key order), sort each bucket by importance, concatenate. Every comparison now happens inside one bucket, so the ordering is total. Regression test sweeps all 6 permutations of [rural road r26, POI r30, correct boulevard r26]; it fails on the old comparator at raw order (1,3,2).

MED R3#2 fixed: resolveBoundary now runs the same searchLadder (canonicalise -> cityGuard) as resolveLocation, prefers an osm_type=relation hit, and fetches that exact entity's polygon via /lookup. Also fixed a latent bug found while doing it: fetchRegionBoundary's OSM-lookup branch SWALLOWED a non-ok response and fell through to an unguarded global name search — same class as R2-HIGH, on the branch no test reached. It now throws.

Reviewer's R3#2 claim (a) is WRONG and was repeated to the human before checking. Verified live: raw 'Quận 3, HCMC' and 'Quận 1, TP.HCM' both resolve to the CORRECT relation (R3819816 / District 1 HCMC) through the old unguarded /search?limit=1. Nominatim's free-form parser handles these. The real defects on that path were the swallowed 429 and the missing country anchor (below), not 'AC-2 fails for VN region names'.

NEW HIGH found by the round-4 live probe (not by any reviewer): a bare region name like 'District 1' resolves to a real polygon in LIBERIA (centroid 6.235,-10.187). cityGuard cannot help — the query names no VN city. resolveConfig auto-frames the camera to the region bbox, so render_map({location:'Ho Chi Minh City', highlight:{regions:['District 1']}}) rendered Liberia while resolved.place still said Ho Chi Minh City. Silent, total wrong-place render in the primary agent call shape.

Fixed the Liberia case with a country anchor, not a distance threshold: resolveLocation/resolveBoundary take expectCountry; resolveConfig passes base.place.country to every highlight point and region. Distance would break the legitimate 'location: Vietnam, highlight: HCMC' (800km apart); country is exact. Hits with no country pass through. Cache key includes the anchor. Verified live: unanchored 'District 1' -> Liberia; anchored -> refused; 'Quận 3, HCMC' -> unchanged.

LOW R3#3 fixed (human chose fix over accept): isAllowedRequest() rejects any request whose Host we do not answer to, and any request bearing an Origin not on the allowlist — a server-to-server MCP client sends no Origin, a web page always does. Defaults to loopback hosts; MAPPOSTER_HTTP_ALLOWED_HOSTS/_ORIGINS for hosted. Binding non-loopback without an allowlist fails closed and logs why. Test drives real requests through node:http (fetch forbids forging Host).

Test-design gap closed: check-vn-addresses.ts now probes resolveBoundary as well as resolveLocation (7 region queries), and every new regression test was verified to FAIL on the pre-fix source before being trusted (9 of 9). Ward-level boundaries still do not exist upstream (Phường Bến Nghé -> no polygon) — documented, not fixed.

Round 4 verify: PENDING-JUDGMENT, evals 12/12 PASS, failedCommands/blocked empty, E12 panel proposes PASS (T3 -> human verdict required). 3 new confirmed findings: 2 MED + 1 LOW, NO HIGH (first round with none). Cap already exceeded once by human authorisation; not looping into round 5 without a second explicit decision.

MED #1 CONFIRMED LIVE by main loop: the round-4 country anchor is bypassed when location is {lng,lat}. resolveLocation's coords branch returns country:'' so anchor=undefined and countryGuard passes everything. Reproduced end-to-end: resolveConfig({location:{lng:106.7,lat:10.78}, highlight:{regions:['District 1']}}) -> camera.center 6.235,-10.187 = LIBERIA. This is the exact bug round 4 fixed, through the door the README recommends for precision. My fix, my hole.

MED #2 confirmed by reading: theme is z.string().optional() at the boundary; resolveConfig assigns it unchecked; getTheme (src/data/themes.ts:273) does THEMES.find(...) ?? THEMES[0] -> silent fallback. `format` by contrast throws 'Unknown format'. `resolved` does not echo theme, so an agent typo ('rubby') yields a midnight-blue poster with zero signal. LOW #3 confirmed: design spec line 55 promises resolved:{center,zoom,place,highlights}; tools.ts:53,64 omit highlights.

Human authorised a scoped round 5 (all 3 findings) and chose reverse-geocoding for the coords anchor, failing closed. Implemented: resolveCountryAt(lng,lat) caches ONLY positive answers (reverseGeocode returns null for both 'no country' and a transient outage — memoizing the latter would be the R2-HIGH bug a fourth time). resolveConfig looks up the anchor only when a highlight is named by string, and throws if the country cannot be determined.

MED #2 fixed: assertTheme() rejects an unknown theme with the list of valid ids, matching how `format` already throws. Previously getTheme() fell back to THEMES[0] and `resolved` did not echo the theme, so an agent typo returned a midnight-blue poster with no signal. LOW #3 fixed: `resolved` now carries `theme` and `highlights:{regions:[{bbox,center}],points:[{lng,lat}]}` per the design spec, so a caller can tell WHICH 'District 1' it got.

8 of the 9 new regression tests confirmed to FAIL on pre-fix source (the 9th asserts no wasted country lookup, guarding a future regression). Live verified at HEAD: coords + bare 'District 1' -> REFUSED; coords + 'Quận 1, TP.HCM' -> 10.775,106.698 (Vietnam); theme 'rubby' -> refused with the id list. Gate: 153 unit + 8 e2e + 2 gated integration, tsc clean on both projects.
